ayahs.1: I swear by the Day of Resurrection—
ayahs.2: and I swear by the self-reproaching nafs—the inner self that accuses itself when it falls short.
ayahs.3: Do people think We cannot reassemble their bones?
ayahs.4: Yes—We can restore them down to their very fingertips.
ayahs.5: Still, people want to deny what lies ahead,
ayahs.6: mockingly asking, 'When is this Day of Resurrection?'
ayahs.8: the moon will lose its light,
ayahs.9: and the sun and moon are brought together,
ayahs.10: on that Day one will cry, 'Where is escape?'
ayahs.12: On that Day every soul will stand before your Rabb.
ayahs.13: Each will be told what they sent ahead and left behind.
ayahs.14: In truth, people will testify against their own nafs,
ayahs.16: Do not move your tongue hastily trying to memorize revelation.
ayahs.17: It is upon Us to gather it and make you recite it.
ayahs.18: When We recite it through Gabriel, follow its recitation closely.
ayahs.19: Then it is upon Us to make its meaning clear.
ayahs.22: Some faces that Day will be radiant,
ayahs.26: No—when the soul reaches the collarbone at death,
ayahs.27: and it is said, 'Is there any healer?'
ayahs.28: the dying person knows departure has come,
ayahs.29: and legs are bound together in the shroud.
ayahs.30: On that Day they are driven to your Rabb.
ayahs.31: This person neither believed nor prayed,
ayahs.33: then strutted back to his people, boastful.
ayahs.35: Again, woe to you—then more woe!
ayahs.36: Do people think they will be left without purpose?
ayahs.37: Were they not once a drop of emitted fluid?
ayahs.38: Then a clinging clot, then shaped and proportioned?
ayahs.39: And from it He made pairs, male and female.
ayahs.40: Is such a Creator unable to bring the dead back to life?
